utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Case Number IT-03-73-I, The Prosecutor versus Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good afternoon, everybody. Mr. Cermak, I want to make sure before we proceed that you can follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand. In other words, that you are receiving interpretation in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Markac, same question to you. I want to make sure that you are receiving interpretation in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am receiving the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good afternoon to you both. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. May it please the Court, Kenneth Scott, senior trial attorney, appearing on behalf of the Prosecutor who I'm happy to have with me today, Madam Carla del Ponte. Also present with the Prosecution is Ms. Laurie Sartorio and our case manager, Diane Boles. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good afternoon to you. Appearances for Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. My name is Cedo Prodanovic. I'm from Zagreb, and I represent Ivan Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good afternoon to you. Appearances for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. I represent Mr. Markac. My name is Miroslav Separovic, and I'm assisted by Mr. Mikulicic from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you too. I want to make sure, Mr. Separovic, that you have been given the consent by the Registrar to represent your client. Because I am informed that for the time being, such consent is forthcoming only with regard to the co-counsel, Mr. Mikulicic. Can I have this confirmed by you, Mr. Separovic, otherwise I will have to request you to leave the courtroom and stay in the gallery and follow the proceedings from there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the administrative difficulties have been dealt with, and I may be present at this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who gave you permission to be present at this hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Registry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please confirm this to me, because I was given other information before I started the sitting, the hearing. Okay. We will now proceed with the Initial Appearance of the accused, Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac, pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Before we do so, let me give a very short outline of the history of this case. Very briefly, the indictment against Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac was confirmed by Judge Parker, a permanent Judge of this Tribunal in Trial Chamber II, on the 24th of February of this year. On the same date, Judge Parker issued first a decision on review of the indictment and order for nondisclosure; and secondly, an ex parte and under-seal warrant of arrest and order for surrender of the two accused. Subsequently, on the 8th of March, my colleague, Judge Parker issued an order lifting the seal of the indictment. He issued also the decision on review of the -- lifting the seal on the decision of the review of the indictment and order for nondisclosure and on the warrants for arrest. And by order of the President of this Tribunal, the following day, that is, on the 9th of March 2004, this case, that is the case against Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac, was assigned to my Trial Chamber, and that is Trial Chamber II. Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac were transferred to the Detention Unit of the -- of this International Tribunal yesterday, that is, Thursday, 11th March 2004. Mr. Cermak and Mr. Markac, in a few minutes' time, I will be giving you the opportunity to enter your pleas to each of the counts contained in the indictment of the 19th February 2004. Before I proceed any further, however, I will be asking you a few questions. And before I ask you the questions, I would like to remind you that you also have a right to remain silent. That is, not to answer any of these questions that I am going to put to you. Mr. Cermak, could I ask you to stand up, please. Again, I want to confirm first and foremost that you are following the proceedings in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm following the proceedings. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I please have your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ivan Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any nicknames by which you are known or you're referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. They call me Cermak on the whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When were you born, your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 19th of December, 1949.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And where were you born, your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born in Zagreb, in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is the address you resided last before you were arrested or before you turned yourself in?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zagreb, Pantovcak, 174. I have another address. It's Dvorac Klokovec in Krapinske Toplica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am now going to inquire from you whether your family are informed about your arrest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my family has been informed, and they are aware of the fact that I surrendered voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are they also aware that you are present here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are. I have told that I am satisfied with everything and that the personnel in the Detention Unit is extremely courteous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you like the Tribunal to notify anyone else from your family about your transfer here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not necessary. Everyone knows that I am here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Markac, again, we are going to go through the whole process with you this time. I want to make sure that you are following what I am saying in a language that you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's proceed with your giving us your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a colonel general. My name is Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are there any nicknames by which you are referred to or known?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 8th of May, 1955 in Djurdjevac, in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could we have your last address immediately prior to your being arrested or prior to your surrender.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tucanova number 3, in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are the members of your family informed about your arrest and also about your presence, transfer and presence, here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are. And they are aware of the fact that I voluntarily surrendered to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any other member of your family that you would like us to inform?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not necessary. Everyone has been informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And now a question to both of you. Are you aware if your embassy, Embassy of Croatia here in The Hague, has been made aware of your presence here in The Hague and about these proceedings? Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they have been informed, and they are present at the hearing. They are in the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they have been informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, as accused before this Tribunal, you enjoy certain rights. These rights are spelled out mainly in two Articles of our Statute. But then there are other rights as well, to which I will be referring, which we come across in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence that have been created by this Tribunal. I will first deal with the rights that are enshrined in our Statute, and I will ask the Registrar to read out the passages from the Statute of the Tribunal that provide you with a certain number of rights, I'm referring specifically to Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute. Following that, we will proceed with the most important formal part of the Initial Appearance, and that has to do with the indictment itself. Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you please read out aloud Articles 20 and 21 of our Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Article 20: Commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. The Trial Chambers shall ensure that the trial is fair and expeditious, and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of the International Tribunal be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him, and transferred to the International Tribunal. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date for trial. The hearings shall be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Article 21: Rights of the accused. All persons shall be equal before the International Tribunal. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing, subject to Article 22 of the Statute. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty, according to the provisions of the present Statute. In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality: (a) to be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him; (b) to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing; (c) to be tried without undue delay; (d) to be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing, to be informed if he does not have legal assistance, of this right, and to have legal assistance assigned to him in any case where the interests of justice so require and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it; (e) to examine, or have examined, the witnesses against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him; (f), to have the free assistance an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal; (g) not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Registrar. And this leads us straight to the indictment. By now, you should have been served with the indictment in your own language. I want to make sure first and foremost that this is so, that I am correct. Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right. We have been provided with a version of the indictment in our own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And while we are at that, can you assure me that you have understood its contents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood the contents of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Colonel Markac, same question to you: Have you received the indictment; and if yes, have you read it and understood it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have received the indictment. I have examined it. And I have understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have asked you these questions because the next step which is perhaps the most important part of today's proceedings will require me to ask of you what kind of plea you want to enter to the charges that have been brought against you. In fact, in accordance with our Rule 62, upon transfer to this Tribunal and in the course of the Initial Appearance, I have certain duties to carry out. One of these is either to read out or have read to you the indictment unless you exempt the Trial Chamber from reading it out, and to satisfy myself that you have understood the indictment. And I also am bound by Rule 62 to inform you that within 30 days of the Initial Appearance, which is taking place today, you will be called upon to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count. This does not mean, however, that we will all have to wait 30 days because the practice is that in the course of the Initial Appearance, the Presiding Judge will direct the question to the accused. In other words, today I may ask you if you are prepared to enter a plea. The understanding is that if you are not prepared to enter your plea today, then you have 30 days maximum within which you could enter the plea. I am informed, but I want to confirm this through your counsel and also through you personally, that you do not wish that we read out in its entirety the indictment. In other words, that you are exempting the Trial Chamber from reading the indictment. Is that so? Stay with counsel for Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the accused Ivan Cermak is aware of his right, and he is waiving his right to have the indictment read out to him. He has understood the indictment, and he will enter a plea on each count without having the indictment read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You confirm that, Mr. Cermak?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do confirm that. It is not necessary to have the indictment read out. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Separovic or Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as General Cermak is concerned, the situation is identical. It is not -- Markac, I apologise. It's not necessary to have the indictment read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: General Markac, do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree with what my attorney has just stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I told you a few minutes ago that I will be proceeding, asking you very soon what you want to -- if you want to plead today and what you want to plead, how you want to plead to the charges that have been brought against you. I want to make sure, however, before I proceed to do this that you have had the opportunity to discuss with your lawyers about this and that you have their advice. Mr. Cermak, have you discussed this matter with your counsel, and are you prepared to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have examined the indictment with my counsel, and I am prepared to enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And General Cermak, same question. Sorry, General Markac. Now I have fallen the same mistake that your lawyer did. General Markac, have you had an opportunity to discuss this matter with your counsel? And if so, are you prepared to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have examined the indictment with my counsel, and I am prepared to enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I address counsel now. Are there any problems that you are aware of which would suggest that the Trial Chamber does not proceed with asking your client, your respective clients, to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there are no objections to continuing with the hearing today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Counsel for General Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as General Markac is concerned, the situation is identical. There are no obstacles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So in view of the waiver that you have confirmed, the whole indictment will not be read out in these proceedings. What will happen is that I will just read out to you the charges contained in the indictment of the Prosecutor of the 19th February 2004. And after each count, I will be asking you separately how -- "how do you wish to plead to that particular charge"? You have these options: You can plead guilty, you can plead not guilty, or you can decide to remain silent. Should you remain silent, then the Trial Chamber has to provide, in accordance with what we have in our Rules. But I don't envisage that problem is going to arise today. And I will start with the first count that is common to both of you. The first count against you both is of criminal responsibility of a crime against humanity consisting in persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, being a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) and Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Cermak, how do you plead to this charge? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General Markac, how do you plead to this first charge? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- Your Honour, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Registrar, for the record, both accused have pleaded not guilty to the first count. The second count against you both is one of a charge of murder as recognised by common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, this being in violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and Article 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Cermak, how do you plead to this charge? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. General Markac, how do you plead to this charge of murder? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Register, for the record, both accused have pleaded not guilty to the second count. The third count against both of you is one of plunder of public or private property, this can a violation of the laws and customs of war punishable under Article 3(e) and Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Cermak, how do you plead to this third count? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General Markac, how do you plead to this third count? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Registrar, for the record, both accused have pleaded not guilty to the third count. The fourth count, again a count which is common to both of you, is one of wanton destruction of cities, towns, and villages, as being a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3(b) and Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Cermak, how do you plead to this count? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And General Markac, how do you plead to this fourth count? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Registrar, for the record, both accused have entered a plea of not guilty to the fourth count. The fifth count, the fifth count is a crime against humanity, consisting in deportation, punishable under Article 5(d) and Articles 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Cermak, how do you plead to this fifth count? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And General Markac, how do you plead to this fifth count?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Registrar, please note for the record that both accused have pleaded not guilty to the fifth count. And we come to the sixth count, which is the penultimate one. This consists of a charge of other inhumane acts, forced displacement, this being a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(1), and Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Cermak, how do you wish to plead to this sixth count? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General Markac, how do you wish to plead to this sixth count?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Registrar, please enter into the records that both accused have pleaded not guilty to the sixth count. And we come to the last count. This is the seventh count, which is one of criminal responsibility for other inhumane acts, being a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(i) and Article 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. And Mr. Cermak, how do you wish to plead to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this seventh count? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And the same question to you, General Markac. How do you wish to plead to this seventh count? Guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Now that you have entered a plea of not guilty to each of the seven counts that have been brought against you by the Prosecutor, I will be instructing the Registrar of this Tribunal, Mr. Holthuis, to fix a date for the appropriate trial -- for the trial when appropriate. This does not mean that you are to expect the trial to commence within the next weeks or within the next months. I'll try to explain to you what the position is. I want you also to understand that in the meantime, you are going to remain in custody until further order. I will be signing an order for your custody at the end of this sitting today. However, in terms of Rule 65, provided the Trial Chamber is satisfied that there are sufficient reasons, you may ask and be granted provisional release in certain circumstances. I do not need to go into details here. I suppose this is too early in the day to talk about provisional release. But I do want to advise you of this possibility, and I am sure that you will be consulting with your lawyers, who I am sure will be giving you the best advice basing themselves on the case law of this Tribunal, which is now pretty much exhaustive on this matter, and provides the guidelines under which usually provisional release is granted. There are some further rights that I would like to draw your attention to before we come to an end. And the first matter that I want to touch upon is the following: The fact that you have entered a plea of not guilty today does not mean that this is an irrevocable step that you have taken. You can, upon the advice of your lawyers, entertain the idea of perhaps coming to some kind of a plea agreement with the Prosecution. There is a procedure to be followed, and your lawyers will be familiar with this and will be able to advise you. Please, do not take what I am saying as an invitation to enter into any kind of plea agreement with the Prosecution. I'm just advising you that this possibility exists and has been made use of by several other detainees that we have here who have found themselves in the same position that you are in today. I also wish to draw your attention to Rule 63 of this Tribunal which provides that questioning by the Prosecutor of an accused, including after the Initial Appearance, shall not proceed without the presence of counsel unless the accused has voluntarily and expressly agreed to proceed without counsel present. If the accused subsequently expresses a desire to have counsel, questioning shall cease immediately and shall only resume when the accused's counsel is present. I'm sure that your lawyers are aware of this provision, and I have no reason to doubt that it will be strictly applied by the Prosecutor. I'm not aware of one single case when the Prosecution did not abide by this Rule. Should there be any such questioning, you ought to know that even if there is a waiver on your part to counsel being present, all this shall be audiorecorded or videorecorded in accordance with the procedure provided for somewhere else in our Rules. And in addition, the Prosecutor at the beginning of the questioning will caution you in accordance with our Rule 42(A)(iii) which basically requires the Prosecution to advise you that you have a right to remain silent and that any statement that you make shall be recorded and may be used in evidence. That is the first matter that I wanted to touch upon. Provisional release, I have already mentioned. The other matter is this: In a few minutes' time, you will be taken back to the Detention Unit. It doesn't mean at all that you are going to be forgotten there, that nothing will happen until we are ready to have the trial. In conformity or in line with the basic requirements of international human rights, especially as they are applied here in Europe, we are required to have what we refer to as Status Conferences, and these are held periodically. Our Rule 65 bis requires that a Status Conference is held at least within 120 days following the previous Status Conference. In the case of today, it means that the first Status Conference must be held not later 120 days starting from today. These Status Conferences serve multiple purposes, the main being: It will give the opportunity, first of all, to you to come face to face with the Pre-Trial Judge; secondly, it will give the Trial Chamber an opportunity to organise between the parties, Prosecution and the Defence, exchanges in order to ensure an expeditious preparation for the trial; and it will also give us, the Pre-Trial Judges, an opportunity to review the case as it happens to -- the situation -- the status of the case as it happens to be at the time; and also, to give you the opportunity to raise issues in relation to the case, including issues that may relate to your state of detention and also to your physical and mental health. I happen to be the Presiding Judge of Trial Chamber II, and therefore I also have a responsibility within the next few days to appoint, designate from amongst the permanent members of my Trial Chamber a Pre-Trial Judge. For the time being, my intention is to assign myself as your Pre-Trial Judge, and I intend to remain your Pre-Trial Judge until I can carry the load, considering the fact that I am in the process of drawing up a judgement in a very difficult case and that I have some other cases. But the other two permanent Judges are also extremely busy, and I think it's only fair at this moment to carry the burden myself. So I will be your Presiding Judge. I will issue the order either later on today, if we are still in time, or on Monday at the latest. There is also one last matter that I wanted to raise, and this I am addressing both to the Prosecution and, as a result, also to you. And I'm referring to Rule 66, which makes it incumbent on the Prosecutor, of course subject to the limitations to the provisions of Rules 53 and 69, to make available to the Defence in a language which the two accused understand within 30 days of -- from today copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought from Judge Parker, as well as all prior statements obtained by the Prosecutor from the accused, if there are any. The second part of Rule 66(A), that is paragraph 2, I don't think we need to go into at this stage, that may come up later on. There are other matters that fall under Rule 66 which, again, we will -- these are pleasures yet to come. We will be dealing with these in the course of the Status Conferences that we will be holding. However, parallel with this obligation of the Prosecutor to hand down to you the material, the supporting material that I have mentioned, within 30 days from today, our Rules in Rule 72 provide that you will have 30 days, and Defence counsel, please take note of this. You will have 30 days after the disclosure by the Prosecution to the Defence of all material and statements referred to in the paragraph which I read out, that is paragraph 66(A)(i), you have 30 days in which to file any preliminary motions in terms of Rule 72. These are limited; namely, the motions I am referring to motions challenging jurisdiction, motions alleging defects in the form of the indictment, motions which seek that the trial does not continue with the two of you being together, but are seeking the severance of the counts joined in one indictment under Rule 49 or to seek separate trials, and also preliminary motions which raise objections based on the refusal of a request for assignment of counsel made under Rule 45. Now, this brings me back to Rule 62, which imposes on me, as Presiding Judge in this Initial Appearance, the duty to satisfy myself that the right of the accused to counsel is respected. Now, I notice from the information that I have that the only problem that there may still be is with regard to Mr. Miroslav Separovic as legal representative and as preferred lead counsel of accused Markac. I think from the looks of it, there are no preliminary problems with regard to Cedo Prodanovic as representing Mr. Cermak, and with regard to Mr. Mikulicic representing as co-counsel, General Markac. The right to a counsel of one's own choosing is respected by this Tribunal, but it's not an absolute right. It doesn't mean to say, for example, that you can bring with you to represent you here anyone you like. We have got our Rules, and the Registrar needs to be satisfied that the lawyers that you suggest satisfy the standards that we have set, both with regard, for example, to qualifications, as well as with familiarity with one or more of the languages of this Tribunal, as well as with ethical standards. In other words, your right to counsel is qualified by these considerations. Also, your right to have counsel paid by this Tribunal is regulated by our Rules which the Registrar will apply. I am here to make sure that your rights are respected, not just these rights, but all other substantial -- substantive and procedural rights. And I want to make myself clear to you: If at any time you feel that your rights are not being fully satisfied, please come back to me, through your lawyers preferably, and bring any such complaints to my attention, and I will attend to them. I also want to make clear that everyone here has his own jurisdiction. The Registrar has his own jurisdiction; the Prosecutor has her own jurisdiction; and we, as the Judges of this Tribunal and Trial Chambers, we have got our jurisdiction. And we can only interfere with some of the decisions of the Registrar in certain limited cases, but even so, if a decision is taken with which you are aggrieved, there is a remedy that our Rules provide for, it being either a direct appeal to the Trial Chamber or a direct appeal to the President of the Tribunal in certain circumstances. As you go along and if there are problems, I'm sure that you are in very capable hands, and your lawyers will advise you accordingly. We are quickly coming to an end. And before we close, I would like to know if on the Prosecution's side there is any matter that you would like to raise. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We will make the disclosures in a timely manner, I'm sure within the 30 days. We anticipate filing later today a motion for protective measures that will enable us to make those disclosures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And I'm sure of your cooperation. I start first with counsel for Mr. Cermak. Is there any matter that you should like to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour. We have no matter which we should like to raise at this stage, except as the Defence counsel for Mr. Cermak I should like to tell you that very soon we will avail ourselves of the rights of Rule 65, the ones that you mentioned, in view of the fact that we consider that we have all the conditions to table a request for provisional release. So we shall be filing that with the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And when you file that, it will be given all due attention. May I remind you that that is a matter which the entire Trial Chamber will need to consider. It's not something that the Pre-Trial Judge alone -- can decide alone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And counsel for General Markac, is there any matter that you would like to raise on behalf of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have nothing at this point in time, no matters to raise, except to say that, like the Defence of General Cermak, we, too, would like to say that we shall be filing a motion similar to the one they shall be doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I want to make sure of one thing before we adjourn. I was made privy to some documentation that you both filed relating to the health, medical condition of your respective clients. For the time being, I only want to know whether that has been resolved to your satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on behalf of the accused Mr. Cermak, I should like to say that I handed over all the medical documents yesterday which indicate that he has troubles with his spine and high blood pressure. And he has been prescribed some medicines for that. And as far as I know, he was examined medically today by a physician, and I think that this procedure is progressing well, that he is being taken care of. If there is something amiss, we shall, of course, address the Court in due course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Cermak, touching on this matter, do you wish to add anything to what your lawyer has just stated? Is there anything else that I can do for you in this area? I'm pretty sure that the matter will be attended to in the most efficient manner by the Detention Unit. But I also want to make sure that you are fully satisfied that your medical condition is being attended to in an efficient manner.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the medical staff in the Detention Unit are extremely courteous and are doing their best for me. I have talked to the medical staff myself, and they have accepted the documents, and I am given my medicines every day, without any problems there. The Registrar will do his best to see that my back is seen to and that I will be given an orthopedic bed because I have troubles with my back. But I thank you for your concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And counsel for General Markac, again, same question, same matter. I also addressed some matters related to your client's health. We don't need to go into details, neither with Mr. Cermak nor with Mr. Markac, even though we're talking of minor things. But has the matter been resolved to your client's satisfaction, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we visited our client this morning, and he informed us that with respect to the medical documentation and treatment, everything is satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General, same question to you: Do you wish to add anything to what has been -- just been stated by your counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to confirm what my counsel has just stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And should there be reason to draw my attention to some requirement that you need to be attended to, please do let me know straight away. Inside the Detention Unit, there are the facilities that allow for medical attention to be given promptly. There may be instances in which one requires medical attention from outside the Detention Unit. That is not always dependable on the Detention Unit itself, but it depends on other circumstances. If there are reasons for concern, please do bring those to my attention. As I said, one of the duties of the Trial Chamber is to ensure that all your rights are fully respected. Is there anything else you would like to raise? I know that your lawyers don't -- don't have any other matter that they would like to raise. If you have other -- yes, Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should just like to thank you for your concern and attention with respect to our health and everything else. Thank you. It is very kind of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So with that, I think we can close this Initial Appearance. As I said, I will give instructions to the Registrar to start planning for this case to come to trial. And in the meantime, on our part, we will also try to start planning for the Status Conferences and with the cooperation for everything, we shall try to accelerate -- we will do our best to accelerate the proceedings to have this case come to trial the earliest possible. I thank you all, and good afternoon to everybody.
